newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen's President Saleh swears in new government.
newsitem.headline: Yemen's President Saleh swears in new government.

text.p: Yemen's new government headed by Prime Minister Faraj Said Bin Ghanem was sworn in on Saturday by President Ali Abdullah Saleh, a government official said.

The 28-member cabinet took the oath of office one day before the new parliament holds its first session after last month's general election, in which Saleh's General People's Congress (GPC) won a landslide victory.

The official told Reuters parliamentarians were expected to re-elect Sheikh Abdullah bin Hussein al-Ahmar as speaker. Al-Ahmar heads the minority Islah party, the GPC's Islamist junior coalition partner in the outgoing government.
"Members of the General People's Congress will vote in favour of re-electing al-Ahmar as speaker," the official said.
Saleh said last week his ruling GPC would run the country alone after it captured 187 seats in the 301-member parliament. Islah, which won 53 seats, said it would join the opposition.
Independents won 54 seats and two opposition parties took a total of five seats. Results for two seats have yet to be announced.
